mainTopic: Is there אבילות on שבת? Proofs from the משנה's wording and from a ברייתא about an אונן on שבת, both of which turn out not to decide the question.
overview: The גמרא presents two opinions: one holds there is some אבילות on שבת, and the other holds there is none. Each side points to a different phrase in the משנה. One side relies on 'עולה' (שבת counts toward the mourning days), and the other relies on 'אינה מפסקת' (שבת does not interrupt them). Each side explains away the other's phrase as wording chosen only to match the סיפא about the רגלים, so the משנה does not settle the question. The גמרא then suggests that the question is an older dispute between תנאים, found in a ברייתא about an אונן whose dead lies before him. On weekdays the אונן has many restrictions, but on שבת he eats normally and keeps the מצוות. רבן גמליאל adds that he is obligated in all of them, and רבי יוחנן explains that the difference is marital relations. The גמרא rejects the link: the ברייתא is about the stage before burial, so both opinions can be explained without deciding anything about an אבל on שבת.

steps.title: Two opinions: is there mourning on שבת or not?
steps.stepSummary: One group holds there is אבילות on שבת; another group holds there is no אבילות on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: [These say:] There is mourning on שבת. And those say: There is no mourning on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out a disagreement about whether a mourner keeps any mourning practices on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view holds that some mourning still applies on שבת, generally understood as private practices no one else would notice. The second view holds that שבת is completely free of mourning. The rest of this section explains where each view comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Mourning, the practices a mourner keeps after a relative's death
There is
There is not
And these (others) say

steps.confusionAlert: Even the opinion of 'יש אבילות בשבת' does not mean full public mourning on שבת. It means only some mourning, of the kind kept privately.

phrases.english: There is mourning on Shabbat,
and those say: There is no mourning on Shabbat.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute: one view says there is some אבילות on שבת, the other says there is none.

steps.title: Each side's source in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The 'there is mourning' side relies on the משנה's word 'עולה' (counts). The 'no mourning' side relies on the words 'אינה מפסקת' (does not interrupt).
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says there is mourning on שבת relies on the משנה teaching that שבת 'counts.' The one who says there is no mourning on שבת relies on the משנה teaching that it 'does not interrupt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that each opinion is reading a different phrase of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says שבת counts toward the seven days of mourning and does not interrupt them. 'Counts' suggests שבת is a real day of mourning, so some mourning applies. 'Does not interrupt' suggests שבת is just a day that doesn't break the count, which fits a day with no mourning at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says
Because it teaches (in the משנה)
Counts, is included toward the seven days
Does not interrupt or cancel the mourning period

phrases.english: The one who says there is mourning on Shabbat,
is because it teaches: 'It counts.'
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: שבת counts as one of the mourning days.

phrases.english: The one who says there is no mourning on Shabbat,
is because it teaches: 'It does not interrupt.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ אֲבֵילוּת בְּשַׁבָּת, דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the textual basis for each opinion in step 1.

steps.title: If mourning applies on שבת, why say it doesn't interrupt?
steps.stepSummary: The 'no mourning' side argues that if mourning really applied on שבת, it would be obvious that שבת doesn't interrupt mourning, so the משנה would not need to say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think there is mourning on שבת, then mourning is actually being kept that day. Do we really need to be told it doesn't interrupt?
steps.whatsHappening: The side that says there is no mourning on שבת attacks the other view by asking why the משנה would bother saying 'it does not interrupt.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A day on which you are actively mourning cannot possibly interrupt mourning, so that would go without saying. The משנה only needs to say 'it does not interrupt' if שבת has no mourning, because then we might think a mourning-free day breaks the count. So the extra phrase shows there is no mourning on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind, if you think that
Now, since already
Is practiced, applies
Is it necessary (to say)?

phrases.english: If it enters your mind
that there is mourning on Shabbat,
now that mourning is practiced on it,
is it necessary to say it doesn't interrupt?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ יֵשׁ אֲבֵילוּת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why 'אינה מפסקת' supports the 'no mourning' view and challenges the other view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that there is אבילות on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If mourning applied on שבת, saying it doesn't interrupt would be unnecessary, so the משנה's wording shows there is no mourning on שבת.

steps.title: But the משנה says שבת counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'no mourning' view: the משנה says שבת 'counts,' which suggests it is a real mourning day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the 'no mourning' side by pointing to the word 'עולה' in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שבת has no mourning at all, why call it a day that 'counts' toward mourning? That word seems to support the other side. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: But then, if so
But look, it teaches

phrases.english: But look, it teaches: 'It counts'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters step 3 by raising the 'יש אבילות' side's source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that there is no אבילות on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'עולה' implies שבת is a genuine day of mourning.

steps.title: 'Counts' was said only to match the second half
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said 'שבת counts' only because its סיפא says the רגלים 'do not count,' so it used parallel wording in the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה wanted to teach in the end part 'they do not count' (about the festivals), it taught in the first part 'it counts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The 'no mourning' side answers that the word 'עולה' is not a real proof. It was chosen to match the wording of the next clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא says the רגלים interrupt mourning and do not count. To set up a neat contrast, the רישא says שבת 'counts.' So 'עולה' only means שבת counts toward the seven days. It does not mean mourning is kept on it, and the 'no mourning' view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because (it wanted to say something else)
The latter clause of the משנה
The first clause of the משנה
They do not count (said of the festivals)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'no mourning on שבת' view proves itself from 'אינה מפסקת' and explains away 'עולה' as wording chosen to parallel the סיפא about the רגלים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: a word in a משנה can be explained as style, used to match a nearby clause, rather than as a source for a ruling.

phrases.english: Since it wanted to teach
in the latter clause 'they do not count,'
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's line about the festivals, which do not count toward mourning.

phrases.english: it taught in the first clause 'it counts.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism (איידי): the word was used to match the סיפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עולה' means שבת is a real mourning day with mourning practices.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עולה' only reflects parallel wording with 'אינן עולים' in the סיפא; no mourning is kept on שבת according to this view.

steps.title: Challenging the view that there is mourning on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'there is mourning' view: if mourning applies on שבת, why does the משנה need to say שבת 'does not interrupt'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says there is mourning on שבת: the משנה teaches that שבת 'does not interrupt' the mourning. Why would it need to say that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the other side. It uses the same kind of question it asked before, just in reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in Step 3, the 'no mourning' side argued that the words 'אינה מפסקת' would be pointless if mourning applied on שבת. The גמרא has already answered the attack on the 'no mourning' side about the word 'עולה.' Now it presses the 'there is mourning' side with that same unneeded phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
But look, it teaches; used to point to a word in the משנה that seems to argue against someone
It does not interrupt (the seven days of mourning)

phrases.english: And according to the one who says there is mourning on Shabbat,
but it teaches 'it does not interrupt'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ אֲבֵילוּת בְּשַׁבָּת, הָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the challenge of Step 4 (pointing to the other side's key word in the משנה), now aimed at the 'יש אבילות' side
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that there is mourning on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שבת is a real mourning day, then saying that it 'does not interrupt' the mourning adds nothing. So the משנה's wording seems to support the 'no mourning' view.

steps.title: The phrase was said only to match the latter clause
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said 'does not interrupt' only because its סיפא says the רגלים 'interrupt,' so it used matching wording in the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה wanted to teach in the later part that the festivals 'interrupt,' it also taught in the first part that שבת 'does not interrupt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the 'there is mourning' view the same way it defended the other side in Step 5. The words are there for parallel style, not to teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side now has a phrase in the משנה that seems to help it: 'עולה' or 'אינה מפסקת.' Each side explains away the other side's phrase as parallel wording. So the משנה alone does not settle the question. That is why the גמרא next looks for an earlier dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of the משנה
The first clause of the משנה
They interrupt; said here about the רגלים ending the mourning period

steps.whatToRemember: Both readings of the משנה are possible. Each side explains away the other's key word as just matching the wording of the סיפא.

phrases.english: Because it wanted to teach in the latter clause 'they interrupt',
it taught in the first clause 'it does not interrupt'.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism: the wording follows the next clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'אינה מפסקת' teaches that שבת is not a mourning day
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase only matches the סיפא's 'מפסיקין' and proves nothing about mourning on שבת

steps.title: Proposing a dispute of תנאים: where the אונן eats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our question matches a dispute between תנאים. It begins quoting a ברייתא about where a person whose dead lies before him may eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute of תנאים. One whose dead relative lies before him eats in another house. If he has no other house, he eats in his friend's house. If he has no friend's house, he makes a partition ten טפחים high. If he has nothing to make a partition with, he turns his face away and eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that our argument is really an older argument between תנאים. It starts quoting the ברייתא it will use. This step is setting up the next moves; the dispute itself comes at the end of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לימא' means 'shall we say': it is a suggestion, not yet a conclusion. This first part of the ברייתא only explains how the person may eat without eating in front of the dead body. Each option is a step down from the one before it.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it is like a dispute of תנאים?
His dead relative lies before him, not yet buried (the stage called אֲנִינוּת)
A partition
Handbreadths

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about an אונן, before the burial. That is not the same as the regular seven days of mourning after burial. The גמרא is using it to learn about how שבת works with mourning in general.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of Tannaim:
One whose dead relative lies before him
eats in another house.
If he has no other house,
he eats in his friend's house.
If he has no friend's house,
he makes himself a partition ten handbreadths high.
If he has nothing to make a partition with,
he turns his face away and eats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה turned out not to settle the matter, the גמרא looks to a dispute between תנאים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the question of mourning on שבת the same as an earlier dispute between תנאים?

steps.title: Weekday restrictions and exemptions of the אונן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists what the אונן may not do at his meal. It also says he is exempt from קריאת שמע, תפלה, תפילין and all the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not recline while eating. He does not eat meat or drink wine. He does not make the ברכה for others or lead a זימון, and others do not make a ברכה or a זימון with him. He is exempt from קריאת שמע, from תפלה, from תפילין, and from all the מצוות in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and describes the אונן's status on a regular weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of rules appear here. First, limits on festive eating: no reclining, no meat, no wine. Second, a full exemption from מצוות, including joining others for ברכות and זימון. This weekday picture sets up the contrast with שבת that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Reclines; the way people ate at a festive meal
Leads the זִימּוּן, the invitation to say ברכת המזון together
Exempt
Reciting the שְׁמַע

phrases.english: And he does not recline and eat,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל בָּשָׂר וְאֵינוֹ שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן,
phrases.english: and he does not eat meat and does not drink wine,
and he does not make the blessing and does not lead the zimun,
phrases.notes: He can't make the ברכה on behalf of others at the meal, and he can't lead the group in ברכת המזון.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו וְאֵין מְזַמְּנִין עָלָיו,
phrases.english: and others do not make a blessing for him and do not include him in the zimun,
and he is exempt from reciting Shema
and from prayer and from tefillin,
and from all the מצוות stated in the Torah.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a weekday, an אונן does not eat festively, does not join others for ברכות or זימון, and is exempt from all מצוות

steps.title: On שבת the אונן eats normally and keeps the מצוות
steps.stepSummary: On שבת the אונן reclines, eats meat, drinks wine, joins ברכות and זימון, and must keep קריאת שמע, תפלה, תפילין and all the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבת he reclines and eats, eats meat and drinks wine. He makes the ברכה and leads a זימון, and others make the ברכה and the זימון with him. He must recite קריאת שמע, daven, wear תפילין, and keep all the מצוות in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the opposite picture for שבת. Every weekday restriction is lifted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item here is the reverse of an item in Step 9. The first תנא's list ends with 'all the מצוות in the תורה.' Keep that phrase in mind, because רבן גמליאל responds to it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated
תפילין (the text mentions them here even on שבת)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't be surprised that תפילין show up on the שבת list. Just learn the ברייתא as it is written here.

phrases.english: But on Shabbat he reclines and eats,
and he eats meat and drinks wine,
and he makes the blessing and leads the zimun,
and others make the blessing and include him in the zimun,
and he is obligated in reciting Shema
and in prayer and in tefillin,
and in all the מצוות stated in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the שבת rules with the weekday rules of Step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת the אונן's restrictions are lifted and he is obligated in the מצוות

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: obligated in these, so obligated in all
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says that since the אונן is obligated in these מצוות on שבת, he is obligated in all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: since he became obligated in these, he became obligated in all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבן גמליאל's statement. This is the opinion the גמרא will compare with the first תנא to find a dispute about mourning on שבת. The explanation of what they argue about comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא already said 'all the מצוות,' so it is not clear yet what רבן גמליאל is adding. His reasoning is 'since he is obligated in these, he is obligated in all.' That points to a wider obligation, and possibly to no mourning at all on שבת. The גמרא will next explain exactly where the two disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because (introduces a 'since this, therefore that' reasoning)
He became obligated
The תנא who gives the second opinion in the ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: The proposed tannaitic dispute depends on the difference between the first תנא and רבן גמליאל. That difference may line up with the two opinions about mourning on שבת.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
Since he became obligated in these,
he became obligated in all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּיב בְּאֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion in the ברייתא; this sets up the comparison proposed in Step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the אונן is obligated in these מצוות on שבת, he is obligated in all of them

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the difference is marital relations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the practical difference between the תנא קמא and רבן גמליאל is whether the אונן may have marital relations on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: the difference between them is marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן clarifies what רבן גמליאל added beyond the תנא קמא: the two disagree about whether an אונן may have marital relations on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא listed many things the אונן does on שבת but did not mention relations, so he holds they stay forbidden. רבן גמליאל said the אונן is obligated in 'all of them,' which includes relations. This gives us a concrete point of dispute that the גמרא can now use.

keyTerms.meaning: Marital relations
There is a difference between them (in practice)
A person whose close relative died and is not yet buried

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Marital relations
is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the תנא קמא and רבן גמליאל from the ברייתא about the אונן on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: תַּשְׁמִישׁ הַמִּטָּה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the practical meaning of רבן גמליאל's statement in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא forbids the אונן to have relations on שבת, and רבן גמליאל permits it.

steps.title: Suggesting the dispute is about mourning on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the תנא קמא holds there is אבילות on שבת and רבן גמליאל holds there is none.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not about this that they disagree: one holds there is mourning on שבת, and the other holds there is no mourning on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the comparison it started in step 8. It says the תנאים in the ברייתא are really arguing about our question: is there mourning on שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations are a private mourning restriction. If the תנא קמא forbids them on שבת, it seems he holds private mourning applies on שבת. If רבן גמליאל permits them, it seems he holds there is no mourning on שבת at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not? (introduces a suggested proof)
They disagree
One master holds
Mourning practices on שבת

phrases.english: Is it not about this that they disagree,
that one master holds: there is mourning on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, who forbids relations.

phrases.english: and one master holds: there is no mourning on Shabbat!
phrases.notes: This is רבן גמליאל, who permits relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יוחנן's clarification to link the ברייתא to the question of אבילות on שבת.
steps.raayaObject: That whether there is אבילות on שבת is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the אונן on שבת, as explained by רבי יוחנן (relations forbidden or permitted).

steps.title: The תנא קמא may forbid only because the dead is unburied
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The תנא קמא may forbid relations only because the dead still lies before him, which does not apply to a regular אבל after the burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Perhaps the תנא קמא said this there only because his dead lies before him. But here, where his dead does not lie before him, he would not forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the תנא קמא does not have to hold that there is mourning on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about an אונן, whose relative is not yet buried. That is a heavier situation. The ban on relations may come from that, not from any rule of אבילות on שבת. So for a regular אבל after the burial, the תנא קמא might agree that relations are allowed on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
Perhaps
He only said it (in that specific case)
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
His dead lies before him (not yet buried)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the ברייתא about an אונן tells us the rules for an אבל. An אונן is before the burial and an אבל is after it, and the גמרא is pointing out that they can have different rules.

phrases.english: From where (do you know this)?
Perhaps he said it only
(that is, the first tanna) there,
because his dead lies before him.
But here,
phrases.notes: "Here" is our case: a regular אבל on שבת, after the burial.

phrases.english: where his dead does not lie before him, no (he would not forbid it).

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first half of the proposed link: the תנא קמא's position.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the תנא קמא as holding that there is אבילות on שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban may come from the special status of an unburied dead (אנינות), not from mourning rules on שבת.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל may permit only because mourning has not begun
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues rejecting the proof. רבן גמליאל may permit relations only because אבילות has not yet started for the אונן, while an אבל after the burial might still be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And perhaps רבן גמליאל said this there only because mourning has not yet started for him. But here, where mourning has started for him, he might also forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes rejecting the proof by showing that רבן גמליאל also does not have to hold that there is no mourning on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבילות begins only after the burial, so an אונן is not yet an אבל. רבן גמליאל may permit relations for that reason. Once the burial has happened and אבילות is in force, he might agree that relations are forbidden even on שבת. Since neither תנא is necessarily talking about our question, the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Still, not yet
Mourning has taken effect
So too, the same here

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to make 'is there אבילות on שבת?' into a dispute between תנאים fails. The ברייתא is about an אונן before burial, and both opinions can be explained by that special stage, without saying anything about an אבל on שבת.

phrases.english: And he said it only
(that is, Rabban Gamliel) there,
because mourning has not yet taken effect on him.
phrases.notes: Mourning starts only once the dead is buried, so an אונן is not an אבל yet.

phrases.english: But here, where mourning has taken effect on him,
so too (he would forbid it).
phrases.notes: He means רבן גמליאל might also forbid relations for a real אבל, even on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in step 14 by explaining רבן גמליאל's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading רבן גמליאל as holding that there is no אבילות on שבת. Together with step 14, this removes the whole proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His leniency may come from the fact that אבילות has not yet begun for an אונן, so it says nothing about an אבל on שבת.
